Events

    Cross-play evaluation

    Every blue pilot plays every red pilot. Metrics follow Kuroswiski et al. with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

    Blue pilots
    Red pilots

    Pick pilots on each side and run an evaluation. A 4×4 matrix at 30 episodes takes a few seconds.

    Metric definitions
    B-score
    Red aircraft neutralized by blue, mean per episode.
    R-score
    Blue aircraft neutralized by red, mean per episode.
    F-score
    B-score minus R-score: the net exchange.
    Mission
    Share of episodes where blue’s mission held (red striker did not reach its target and blue was not wiped out).
    Missile eff.
    Blue hits divided by blue missiles fired, pooled over episodes.
    Return
    Blue team cumulative reward per episode, using the configured reward weights.

    Weapon engagement zone

    Max launch range (Rmax, dashed) and no-escape range (NEZ, solid) the agents observe, by where the target points relative to us, with the target on our nose. Derived by flying the missile model, not by formula.

    Validate against the missile model

    Fires one missile per case from a fixed range at a non-maneuvering target and measures hits. Same recipe as python -m bace.experiment wez.

    Range card, co-altitude, target on the nose

    Hit rate vs launch range

    Dashed verticals: the Rmax agents observe for each curve. A consistent model shows the hit rate falling to zero close to its dashed line. Launches are delayed beyond the 50 NM radar range, so the sweep stops at 48 NM.

    Generic missile parameters

    Scripted opponent search

    Evolves the three FSM thresholds (shot distance, crank, break) against a growing pool of opponents, as in the paper’s baseline enemy selection. Keep some noise or jitter: without them every episode of a pairing is identical.

    Fitness by generation

    Elites

    Run a search to find elite opponents. Add them as pilots for Simulate and Evaluate.

    Environment self-test

    Checks the properties an RL benchmark relies on: reproducibility, observation contract, no privileged information, reward accounting, and speed. Everything runs on this machine in WebAssembly.
